persons.name: Bora Özkent
persons.digest:
Bora Özkent reads the sharp selloff after the September CPI calmly: core inflation came in 0.1 points above expectations, but more than half of the headline rise comes from gasoline, up 9.1% on the month, and the rest from rent-driven shelter. Excluding shelter he calculates core at 0.13% on the month and sees no reason for the Fed to hike in October; the market also prices October hike odds at around 28.7%.

He does not read the 10-year yield falling from its 5.31-5.32% peak to 5.086%, breakeven inflation expectations barely moving, and bond buying accompanying the equity selloff as an inflation panic. Behind the tech selloff he sees Anthropic's revenue, which fell slightly short of expectations despite 46% quarterly growth against a $2 trillion valuation, and the memory worries in South Korea. The dates he will watch are the October 28 Fed decision, October 29 PCE and November 10 CPI; in his own portfolio he is holding rather than selling because of taxes and reminds viewers of tax-loss harvesting for stocks sitting at a loss.

items.title: Is US Inflation on Fire?
items.summary: Bora Özkent argues that the 0.1-point core miss in the September CPI scared markets more than it should have. Headline was 0.6% m/m and 3.7% y/y, in line with expectations; core was 0.3% m/m and 2.6% y/y, 0.1 point above. More than half of the headline rise comes from gasoline, up 9.1% on the month (34.2% y/y), which he ties to the Iran war and refinery capacity limits; the rest is rent-driven shelter. Excluding shelter, core is 0.13% m/m and below 2% annualized. The hawkish reading points to airfares (22.4% y/y) and fuel costs leaking into services; the dovish reading notes rents and owners' equivalent rent are calm and market rents are lower. The 10-year yield fell from a 5.31-5.32% peak to 5.086% while 10-year breakeven inflation stayed at 2.35%; October hike odds are 28.7% and a December hike is priced (65.3% for the 4-4.25% range). He cites Anthropic's 46% quarterly growth, slightly below expectations ahead of a $2 trillion valuation, and memory worries in South Korea as the cause of the tech selloff. Calendar: October 28 Fed, October 29 PCE, November 10 CPI; his own portfolio is about 10% below its peak and he is not selling because of taxes.

assets.note: Nasdaq fell as much as 2%; he points to Anthropic news and memory worries as the cause of the tech selloff.
